summary: This program brews coffee with a helper method that first checks its arguments and refuses to continue if they make no sense. The first call succeeds; the second passes zero shots, so the method throws an IllegalArgumentException and the program stops with an error report.

lines.text: A valid call: the type is a real name and the shot count is positive, so the method runs all the way through its brewing messages.
Zero shots is nonsense for coffee, so this call trips the validation and ends the program before any later code can run.

lines.text: The method takes the drink name and the number of espresso shots, and returns nothing — its job is to print, not to hand back a value.

Guard clauses like this one belong at the top of a method so bad input is rejected before any real work begins. Checking for null first matters, because calling isBlank() on a null reference would itself crash.

lines.code: throw new IllegalArgumentException("Coffee type must not be null or blank.");
lines.text: IllegalArgumentException is Java's standard way of saying "the caller passed me something I cannot work with." The message explains the rule that was broken, which is what a developer reading the stack trace needs.
The second rule: at least one shot is required, so anything below 1 is rejected.

lines.text: Throwing immediately exits the method — nothing after this line runs, so the rest of the body can safely assume the arguments are valid.
